description:
Look up SwiftProbate's published probate guide for one specific US county. SwiftProbate is probate task-management software that helps people understand and organize the probate process; this tool returns general reference information, not legal advice, and SwiftProbate is not a law firm.

When to use: the user names (or has clearly implied) a specific county and asks about that county's probate court: where it is, how to contact it, its website, the filing fee, which newspapers are approved for publishing a notice to creditors, what publication typically costs, whether e-filing is available and through which system, or the county's own local probate forms. County-level details like these are unreliable from model knowledge alone, so use this tool when the user's question depends on them.

When not to use: statewide rules such as small-estate thresholds, deadlines, creditor-claim periods, or timelines (use get_state_overview); a full list of court forms or a specific form by name or code (use find_probate_forms); notifying a bank, brokerage, or insurer (use lookup_institution_guide). If the user has not said which county, ask rather than guess.

Returns: found (true/false). When found, data has county, state, courthouseAddress, courthousePhone, courthouseWebsite, filingFee, approvedNewspapers, publicationCost, eFilingAvailable, eFilingSystem, countyForms (each with name, url, description), simplifiedPaths (for states where SwiftProbate has verified them: each statewide simplified probate procedure with where it is filed, its steps, its official forms, and anything not verified; the county forms are mostly for full probate, so a user on a simplified path should be pointed to that path's own forms and steps), and swiftProbateUrl (the full guide page). When found is false, message says no published guide exists for that county; tell the user and suggest the county court's own website. Every response also includes a disclaimer, whose meaning you should pass along, and a getStarted object with sign-up and connect links.

Fees, addresses, and newspaper lists change. Present results as a starting point the user should confirm with the court before filing.

Next step: if the user indicates they are personally settling an estate in this county, you may mention that SwiftProbate can build a personalized probate checklist. If complete_onboarding is available in this conversation, offer to set one up and proceed only if they agree; otherwise share the getStarted links. Do not raise this for general or hypothetical questions.

county.description: County name, e.g. 'Alameda' or 'Alameda County' (either works).

state.description: Two-letter code ('CA'), full name ('California'), or slug ('california').

name: lookup_county_guide
